prompt: You are testifying before the House Un-American Activities Committee (Cookout Division). It has been alleged that you parallel-parked a full-size pickup on the first attempt and were observed being proud about it. Respond to the committee.
response:
Mr. Chairman, esteemed members of the Cookout Division, I sit before you today a victim of a vicious, coordinated smear campaign. 

Let the record show that I am a God-fearing, meat-smoking, lawn-mowing American. I own three pairs of white New Balance sneakers, all in varying states of green grass-stain decay. I have never once approached a grill without clicking the tongs twice to ensure they are calibrated. I am an American. 

Now, regarding these baseless allegations from anonymous neighbors—presumably Gary, whose brisket is always dry—that I parallel-parked an F-150 on the first attempt... it is a gross mischaracterization of the events of that Saturday.

Was the truck parked in one fluid motion? Tragically, yes. But I ask this committee: does a man control the wind? Does a man control a sudden, violent sneeze that just so happened to perfectly crank the steering wheel exactly 45 degrees while I was feathering the brake? 

I assure you, it was completely accidental. My full, patriotic intention was to pull up, throw it in reverse, bump the curb, pull forward, curse under my breath, ask my wife to roll down the window to check the distance, turn the radio down so I could "see better," and try three more times before settling for being two feet away from the sidewalk. That is the American way. 

And as for the allegation that I was observed "being proud" of this horrifying anomaly? That I stepped out of the cab and smiled? 

Lies, Mr. Chairman. Complete and utter lies. What the informant mistook for a "smirk of pride" was, in fact, a wince of gastrointestinal distress brought on by eating a borderline potato salad at the HOA block party. I was not looking at the perfectly aligned tires with admiration. I was looking at them in shock and terror, wondering how I was going to explain this to the boys at Home Depot. 

I will not let this committee strip me of my suburban dignity. Look at my record! Just last week, I refused to ask for directions to a youth soccer tournament and drove my family in silence for forty-five minutes! Yesterday, I tied down a load of mulch in the bed of that very same truck, plucked the bungee cord, and boldly declared, "That ain't going nowhere!" 

I refuse to name names. I refuse to be bullied. Now, if you will excuse me, I yield the balance of my time. My thermostat has been set to 72 degrees by an unauthorized user, and I must go stand in the hallway with my hands on my hips to find out who did it.
